_note: Single source of truth for curated sites. lat/lon in degrees, longitude East-positive. 'snap' = move to the highest LOLA terrain within N metres (rim crests / peaks). 'tryDate' = best landing date found for that spot (the app jumps there when it's picked). 'rim' = start from the highest point on that crater's rim (catalogued centre + diameter). Coordinates marked approx are region centres, not exact landing points.

sites.name: Shackleton–de Gerlache Ridge
sites.blurb: The ridge connecting Shackleton and de Gerlache craters — one of the most persistently sunlit spots on the Moon.

sites.name: Shackleton Crater Floor
sites.blurb: A permanently shadowed region ~2.8 km below the rim. Water ice may survive here because the Sun never rises above the crater wall.

sites.name: Malapert Massif
sites.blurb: A 5 km-high mountain and Artemis III candidate region. Tall enough to see Earth more often than the lowlands around it.

sites.name: de Gerlache Rim
sites.blurb: NASA Artemis III candidate region on the rim of de Gerlache crater. Approximate point: the highest spot on the rim, found from NASA LOLA terrain.

sites.name: Haworth
sites.blurb: NASA Artemis III candidate region beside Haworth, a large permanently shadowed crater. Approximate point: the highest spot on its rim.

sites.name: Chang'e-7 target (Shackleton rim)
sites.blurb: China's Chang'e-7 mission is planned to land near the sunlit rim of Shackleton crater to look for water ice. Approximate point: the highest spot on the rim.

sites.name: Pick 1: Malapert Shoulder
sites.blurb: Balanced pick on the shoulder of Malapert. Power and Earth at the same time about 60% of the year, more than any official candidate here. Earth never sets. Best landings in 2027: Sep 8, Oct 7 and Nov 6 (about 19 days of light each). Permanent shadow, possible ice, about 5 km away. Found by Rimlight from NASA LOLA sunlight, Earth-visibility, shadow and slope maps (scripts/find_picks.py).

sites.name: Pick 2: Nobile Plateau
sites.blurb: Balanced pick near Nobile crater. Power and Earth at the same time about 60% of the year, and Earth never sets. Best landings in 2027: Sep 30, Oct 30 and Nov 29. A permanently shadowed crater (possible ice) is about 1 km away. Found by Rimlight from NASA LOLA sunlight, Earth-visibility, shadow and slope maps (scripts/find_picks.py).

sites.name: Pick 3: Pole Ridge
sites.blurb: Power pick on a flat ridge 20 km from the pole. Sunlit 77% of the year. Land on Oct 9, 2027 and the Sun stays up for 47 days, with Earth in view almost all of the first two weeks. Permanent shadow, possible ice, is under 1 km away. Found by Rimlight from NASA LOLA sunlight, Earth-visibility, shadow and slope maps (scripts/find_picks.py).

sites.name: IM-2 Athena (Mons Mouton)
sites.blurb: Intuitive Machines' 2025 lander on the Mons Mouton plateau — the southernmost landing attempt to date.

sites.name: IM-1 Odysseus (Malapert A)
sites.blurb: First US soft landing since Apollo (Feb 2024), near Malapert A crater.

sites.name: Chandrayaan-3 Vikram
sites.blurb: India's 2023 lander — the first near the south polar region. It ran for one lunar day, then froze in the lunar night.

sites.name: Luna-25 target (Boguslawsky)
sites.blurb: Russia's planned 2023 landing site. The spacecraft crashed before reaching it.

sites.name: Apollo 11 (Tranquility Base)
sites.blurb: Equatorial landing site: the Sun climbs high, and Earth sits almost still in the sky.

sites.name: Apollo 15 (Hadley–Apennine)
sites.blurb: Mid-latitude site at the foot of the Apennine mountains.

sites.name: Apollo 17 (Taurus–Littrow)
sites.blurb: The last crewed landing (1972).

sites.name: SLIM (Shioli crater)
sites.blurb: JAXA's 2024 precision lander. It touched down upside-down, so its solar panels only worked when the Sun was in the west.

sites.name: Blue Ghost M1 (Mare Crisium)
sites.blurb: Firefly's 2025 lander. It operated a full lunar day and filmed sunset from the surface.

sites.name: Chang'e 4 (Von Kármán)
sites.blurb: The first far-side landing. Earth never rises here, so every bit of data goes through the Queqiao relay satellite.

sites.name: Chang'e 6 (Apollo basin)
sites.blurb: The first sample return from the far side (2024). It also had no direct-to-Earth link.
